summary: Tiziana Pontillo is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.

Todd A. Gibson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University, earning a PhD by 1991, with teachers György Kara and Yonten Gyatso, and committee members Christopher I. Beckwith, Elliot Sperling, Larry Moses, and Michael L. Walter.

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University (~1977–1984) and under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (~1987–1988), later becoming Murray Distinguished Professor at the College of the Holy Cross (~1990).

Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts as a lecturer at Tohoku University (~1925–1934) and at the University of Tokyo (~1946).
Tokio Takata specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1968 to 1975 and held an academic post there from ~1983 to 2014.
Tokugen Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1934 to 1937 and later served as a professor (教授) at Komazawa University.

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara. He held posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and as Dozent at Toyo University (1891).

Tokuryu Yamauchi studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University (~1912–1915). He held posts at Kyoto Institute of Technology (~1949–1952), Kyoto University of Education (~1953–1965), and Ryukoku University (~1965–1970).
Tom De Rauw is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Ghent University (~2004–2008) under the supervision of Ann Heirman.

Tom J. F. Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Lausanne (~1992–2011) and held the Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary (~2008).
Tomoaki Tsuchida is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral committee studies by 1986 under Benjamin I. Schwartz, Masatoshi Nagatomi, and John B. Carman.

Tomohisa Ikeda specializes in Sinology and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1973), he held posts at Kōchi University (~1973–1980), Gifu University (~1980–1988), the University of Tokyo (~1988–2003), and Daito Bunka University (~2003–2013).

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (~-1985), and held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–1999) and the University of Michigan (1999).
Tomoo Fujimaru is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held posts at the Hongwanji Comprehensive Research Institute and as director (主事) at the University of Tokyo Young Buddhist Association.
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and has held a post as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Kyoto University.
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University and held an appointment there as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師).

Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as a special researcher at the JSPS (~1996–1998), as an assistant professor (助教授) at Chikushi Jogakuen University, and at Hiroshima University.

Tomy Augustine is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Madras, Banaras Hindu University, and under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal. He held a post at Salesian College.

Toni Huber is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Canterbury (~1989–1993). He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (~1999–2004) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~2004–2021).

Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976) and held faculty posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).
